subject: chemical
audience: FE Chemical candidates and chemical engineering students
title: The 70% Conversion That Produced Only 50% Yield
featured_title: THE 70 PERCENT CONVERSION THAT PRODUCED ONLY 50 PERCENT YIELD

presentation.challenge: Seventy percent of A reacted, but only fifty percent of the feed became the desired product B. Conversion was not the same as yield.

practice.primary_question: How are conversion, desired-product yield, and selectivity distinguished for parallel reactions?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Reporting reactant conversion as desired-product yield without accounting for reactant consumed by undesired parallel reactions.

case_dna.target_misconception: If 70% of reactant A disappears, the desired-product yield must also be 70%.
case_dna.why_plausible: Conversion measures reactant disappearance, so it can be mistaken for the fraction that becomes the desired product.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: On a 100 mol A feed basis, 70 mol A reacts but only 50 mol B forms while 20 mol C forms. Conversion is 70%, desired B yield on feed is 50%, and B/C selectivity is 2.5.
case_dna.corrected_model: Conversion tracks reactant consumption; yield and selectivity track how reacted material is distributed among products. Definitions must be stated explicitly.

problem_statement: Use a 100 mol A feed basis. Parallel reactions convert A one-for-one to desired product B or undesired product C. At the outlet, 30 mol A remains, 50 mol B has formed, and 20 mol C has formed. Define conversion as moles A reacted per mole A fed, desired-product yield as moles B formed per mole A fed, and selectivity as moles B formed per mole C formed. Calculate all three quantities.
fixed_constraints: Yield basis is B formed per A fed

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Reactant disappearance did not guarantee desired product formation.
gates.prompt: Which metric measures how much A disappeared, independent of where it went?

options.label: Conversion uses A reacted; yield uses B formed per A fed; selectivity uses B/C
options.reason: These are the explicit definitions stated for this case.

options.label: Conversion, yield, and selectivity are all equal when stoichiometry is 1:1
options.reason: Parallel reactions can consume A without forming the desired product.

options.label: Yield is automatically B/A reacted even when another basis is specified
options.reason: Yield definitions vary, so the stated basis must be followed.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the desired-product yield
gates.prompt: Using the stated feed basis, enter the B yield as a percentage.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Close the outlet material accounting
gates.result: The desired B yield on the stated feed basis is 50%.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove conversion, yield, and selectivity
gates.prompt: The desired-product yield is 50/100×100. Enter percent.
gates.hint: Do not replace the desired-product amount with the total amount of A reacted.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The undesired pathway explains the gap

cards.text: A reacted=100-30=70 mol, so conversion is 70%.
Only 50 mol B formed, so desired B yield on A fed is 50%.
B/C selectivity=50/20=2.5 mol B per mol C.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the reactor-performance note
report: C1. Seventy moles of A reacted.
C2. Fifty moles of desired B formed.
C3. Therefore the desired-product yield is 70%.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This follows from 100 mol fed minus 30 mol remaining.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated desired-product amount.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It substitutes reactant conversion for the stated desired-product yield definition.

evidence_choices.label: Yield=50 mol B/100 mol A fed=50%
evidence_choices.reason: This uses the yield basis explicitly defined in the problem.

correction.template: Conversion is {conversion}%, desired B yield is {yield}%, and B/C selectivity is {selectivity}.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Improve selectivity while keeping conversion at 70%
gates.constraint: Keep 70 mol A reacted, allow only B and C products with 1:1 stoichiometry, and increase B/C selectivity to 4:1.

options.label: Form 56 mol B and 14 mol C, giving 56% B yield
options.reason: A 4:1 split of 70 reacted moles gives 56 mol B and 14 mol C.

options.label: Form 70 mol B and 17.5 mol C
options.reason: That would require 87.5 mol A reacted, violating the fixed 70% conversion.

options.label: Form 40 mol B and 10 mol C
options.reason: Only 50 mol products would be accounted for, not the 70 mol A reacted.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Separate conversion from selectivity in a new outlet
gates.prompt: From 100 mol A fed, 80 mol reacts to form 60 mol B and 20 mol C. What is B/C selectivity?

options.reason: That is the reactant conversion on the 100 mol feed basis.
That is the desired-product yield on the feed basis.

gates.explanation: Conversion, yield, and selectivity answer different performance questions.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the reaction-performance metrics
gates.confirmation: I confirm that conversion measures reactant disappearance, while yield and selectivity require explicit product-based definitions.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Reactant conversion was reported as desired-product yield.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Twenty moles of A were consumed by the undesired parallel pathway.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Calculate conversion, yield, and selectivity from their stated bases separately.

seo.seo_title: Conversion vs Yield vs Selectivity: Parallel Reactions | FE E-070
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Chemical Case E-070: 70% A conversion can still give only 50% desired-product yield when a parallel reaction forms an undesired product.
seo.excerpt: High conversion does not automatically mean high desired-product yield. Parallel reactions can send reacted material to unwanted products.
seo.direct_answer: On a 100 mol A feed basis, 30 mol A remaining means 70% conversion. If 50 mol B and 20 mol C form, the stated desired B yield is 50/100=50%, while B/C selectivity is 50/20=2.5.

faqs.q: Is conversion the same as product yield?
faqs.a: No. Conversion measures how much reactant is consumed; yield measures desired product according to a stated basis.

faqs.q: What is B/C selectivity when 50 mol B and 20 mol C form?
